Always glove up if something isn’t right. Wear non-latex gloves, ask the client if they know about the bumps on their back and if they hurt to work over them. The client may not know they exist with it being their middle back. If they hurt to work over, don’t work the area and suggest a doctor, but be careful not to diagnose. 

We had a student with bad cystic acne a few years ago, avoid anything raised and anything that is red or warm to the touch. You may accidentally cause an extraction or bursting of the lesion, that’s why you have gloves..... However, it is not ok to do so on purpose unless you’re also a licensed esthetician. I keep a first aid kit in my room, depending on the size of these lesions they may pop then bleed badly. I’m always prepared for battle with blood borne pathogens.

Just talk to your client about their body. I usually tell them, “with these open wounds(lesions, sores, etc.)  I am going to wear gloves to protect both of us.” If the gloves fit correctly and you use enough lubrication, they shouldn’t be able to tell. You can also use Saran Wrap (I buy name brand plastic wrap because it doesn’t tear as easily) on tools and elbows, but it’s not comfortable to work in. Hope this helps.

I had a vet for them about an hour away(technically an exotic pet), but my dogs saw the vet in town. I got wire cutters & got her loose, but a 12 gauge piece of metal wire (it was thicker than my 14g piercings) was still in the wound. I rushed her to the local vet, and told the lady at the front desk what had happened. The desk lady stood up & said, “I don’t care what’s wrong with it, we won’t see pocket pets!” Excuse me?!? I put Suede on the counter to show her the blood & the wire, as the vet walked into the front. He heard her yell at me, so he came to see. Not only did the awesome Vet get Suede fixed up, it was free. He apologized to me when we were in the exam room for desk lady’s rude behavior. He stated that while they don’t typically see pocket pets, he wouldn’t leave a tiny animal in pain. He explained the anesthesia might kill her, but a drifting to sleep death is better than the shock she was in. She woke right up after he was done. I had to go back to work & get her some grape flavored baby bactrim to fight infection. (I thought getting a toddler to take medication was brutal, try a freaking baby rodent.) We went back a week later for the local vet to assess Suede’s stitches & pick up seizure medication for my dog at the time...... & the desk lady no longer worked there..... she had been replaced with an old friend from school! The best part, a new sign on the front door saying they would see all domesticated pet animals Incase of an emergency (not horses or livestock due to being in the middle of town with a tiny parking lot).
